reason: The cited evidence shows that Mo, Si, and B can refine microstructures and improve wear or corrosion resistance individually, but no passage demonstrates simultaneous wear-corrosion resistance governed by a stable, dense, refined microstructure, nor does any directly compare the proposed alloy-plus-processing combination against a stainless steel baseline under combined harsh conditions. The mechanism linking reduced defects and passive film stability is not explicitly supported by the cited texts.
premises: Addition of Mo, Si, or B refines and stabilizes the microstructure of HEAs
A refined, stable, dense microstructure enhances resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion
Processing techniques like laser cladding or vacuum arc remelting promote grain refinement and lattice distortion
The mechanism involves reducing defect formation and increasing passive film stability
These effects lead to improved durability over conventional alloys like stainless steels
